thread:
nina: FYI I dug into a billing ticket from ACME - they say their dedicated pool shows more consumption than our console route metrics indicate. Looks related to fncall validation rejects.
tom: timeline? what does the trace show?
nina: trace shows: request hits r1-large -> model returns fncall payload -> validator rejects due to extra top-level field -> router retries to r2-small -> success. Billing record only has r2-small.
priya: do we currently emit any "reject" events downstream?
kevin: validator logs the error but we don't surface rejects into the streaming event graph used by billing. That graph only consumes 'final_response' messages.
priya: that explains the gap. Two options I see: 1) enrich emitted final_response with a sidecar field like "rejects": [{route, reason}], or 2) emit a separate reject_event that billing joins on request_id.
tom: option 1 is simpler for consumers but means the billing message size grows. Option 2 keeps messages small but requires joins in the pipeline.
nina: ACME wants an "audit path" they can download per request, not just aggregated counts. So we need to ensure the timeline is reconstructable.
kevin: what about a hybrid: emit a cheap reject marker in final_response (like attempted_route and error_class) and also stream full reject_event to the rich events topic for backfill/console inspection. Keeps billing light.
priya: that works. We should also mark whether the reject incurred charge or not. Right now the reject path still uses GPU cycles. For customer billing we probably should attribute cost to attempted route, not silently to fallback.
tom: I worry about customers gaming this by purposely failing validation to push cost upstream. Maybe add a billing policy: validation_rejects are marked as "audit_only" for the first N retries, and only contribute to quota if server actually executed tokens on the fallback > X ms.
kevin: we have token-level cost tags from the runtime. We can compute charge attribution server-side: if attempted route executed > 0 tokens, attribute proportional cost to attempted route. But we must surface both attempted and final routes for observability.
nina: OK. Implementation plan proposal: router emits reject_event with fields: request_id, attempted_route, error_class, executed_tokens_estimate. Also add attempted_route and error_class as small fields on final_response. Rate-limit reject_event emission per org to avoid bursts.
priya: we need a public-safe mapping for error_class. Don't expose internal enum names. Expose one of [bad_shape, missing_required, type_mismatch, auth_error, other].
tom: console work: add a timeline panel in request inspector that pulls from the rich events topic and falls back to attempted_route in final_response when no reject_event exists. Make timeline queries limited to 7 days by default.
kevin: billing pipeline change: if reject_event exists, billing transform should split cost based on executed_tokens_estimate. If not, fallback to attributing all cost to final_route (current behavior) but mark as "attribution_uncertain". Add a flag to backfill historical data for customers who request it.
nina: safety: rollout behind two flags: router.reject_emit (default off) and billing.reject_consume (default off). We'll enable router in canary first.
priya: sampling: emit full reject_event 100% for orgs flagged for audit, otherwise sample 5% globally. Also emit attempted_route on final_response always (tiny payload).
tom: what about tests? We need an integration test that simulates fncall-invalid -> reject_event emitted -> billing pipeline receives both messages and splits attribution correctly. Also unit tests for request_id propagation.
kevin: add a lint rule: validator returns canonical error_class only via mapping util so all services use same public names. Put mapping in docs and SDKs.
nina: ownership: eng-runtime (router + validator) implements emit and attempted_route on final_response. eng-platform (billing) implements consumption logic. console team implements timeline.
priya: timeline for MVP: router patch (2 days), billing transform (3 days), console timeline stub (4 days) that shows attempted_route from final_response. Full timeline from rich events in 2 weeks.
nina: I opened ticket ENG-914 for router work and ENG-915 for billing. CONS-420 for console timeline MVP.
kevin: alerting: create an SLO for attribution accuracy and fire alert when >1% of requests in a minute have attribution_uncertain. Also create internal dashboard showing attempted_vs_final counts per route.
tom: operational guardrails: add backpressure protection on reject_event topic. If downstream lag > 5m, router should stop emitting full reject_event and only include attempted_route on final_response.
priya: agreed. We'll implement a token-bucket per-org limiter plus global lag watch.
nina: example reject_event payload for PR description: ```json
{
  "request_id": "req_2026xyz",
  "event": "validation_reject",
  "attempted_route": "r1-large",
  "error_class": "bad_shape",
  "executed_tokens_estimate": 12
}
```
kevin: note: executed_tokens_estimate is best-effort. For accuracy we can later integrate per-op instrumented token counters.
tom: who will pick up ENG-914? nina?
nina: picking it up, will open PR today. tagging @kevin and @priya for review.
console-bot: CONS-420 created and assigned to priya.
priya: I'll stub the UI using attempted_route field first.
nina: thanks everyone. Let's reconvene after canary deploy.
ingest-bot: routing canary deployment scheduled for tomorrow 03:30 UTC.
kevin: will monitor.
priya: I'll add integration tests to the billing repo and link the PR.
frank: (joins late) one more ask: expose a CSV export for customers of the request timeline within console for audit purposes.
priya: adding to CONS-420 as an optional follow-up.
kevin: done.
nina: end
summary: Plan to fix misattribution from fncall validation rejects by emitting lightweight attempted_route on final_response and optional detailed reject_event into rich events topic; billing will split cost when reject_event present, with rollout behind feature flags, sampling, rate-limiting, and operational backpressure guards; console will show a timeline and CSV export later.
